Topic 3.1: Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary, part of Family Suggested vocabulary: father, mother, sister, brother, baby, aunt, uncle, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce words correctly? 2. How can we listen attentively during conversations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication: learner listens keenly and actively and show understanding as they respond to simple one -directional instructions

related to the theme.

● Self-efficacy: learner’s knowledge of their family is enhanced as they use dialogues/rhymes/tongue twisters/ language games/ songs

about family.

Values:
Respect: promoted as learners show positive regard for self and others as they role play during the lesson.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Gender issues awareness is nurtured as the learner shows appreciation of gender and interpersonal relationship as they talk about

different family members.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Kiswahili Language Activities: as learners identify the target letters of the alphabet with their sound appropriately.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
